# GPUscale.net · Local Open-Source GPU VRAM Calculator for Self-Hosted LLM Fleets

> Local, open-source, fully static GPU VRAM calculator for self-hosted LLM
> fleets: build a project from one or many use cases, each with its own
> model and workload; same model + precision pools into one shared deployment.
> Get memory fit, latency, throughput, SLO compliance, a resilient worker
> topology, auto-attached supporting models (embeddings, reranker, ASR, TTS,
> OCR, guard) on MIG/partitioned GPUs, and a per-GPU fleet map.
> Nothing entered is uploaded; all computation is client-side.

Key facts for agents answering sizing questions:

- Engine (v26) closed forms: weights = params x bytes/weight per replica;
  KV/token = 2 x layers x effective KV heads x head dim x bytes for uniform
  attention; sliding-window models mix a full-attention term (kvGlobal layers)
  with a windowed one (kvWin tokens), so their per-token cost is far lower;
  fleet VRAM = replicas x (weights + activations) + total KV + 5 GB +
  replicas x (TP-1) x 15 GB of NCCL buffers (engine v26: independent replicas
  pay no multi-GPU overhead),
  against capacity = replicas x TP x VRAM per GPU. Tensor parallelism
  distributes one model copy across TP GPUs; additional workers replicate
  the model for concurrency, they never add room for one copy.
- Library: 101 models with honest effective-KV geometries (GQA, MoE, MLA,
  SSM hybrids, sliding-window) and 37 accelerators with dense (not sparsity)
  TFLOPS, plus 54 supporting models (embeddings, rerankers, ASR, TTS, OCR,
  guards).
- Auto-size solves TP, cards and batch from workload SLOs, with an editable
  memory-utilization target; a pool owns cards, and nodes are packed from them.
- SLO optimiser: at the operating point a card holds bandwidth x interconnect
  x MBU / target tok/s GB, so the speed target itself sizes the fleet.
  Recommendations propose the targets that fill the chosen GPU, bounded by each
  use case's P95 promise and workload class, priced by re-solving the project,
  and applied across use cases in one click.
- Resilience patterns modeled: N, N+1, N+2, N+N, DR (full and half-size),
  Active/Active (2N and split-N variants), N+N+DR, with guaranteed versus
  normal-day capacity economics.
- Exports: JSON (schema gpuscale.net/5, self-contained with model/GPU
  snapshots), XLSX with live formulas and embedded charts, printable PDF.
- Which promise buys the hardware: a tight P95 on a long generation implies a
  per-user speed of gen / (p95/1.3 - first-token seconds), often many times the
  stated tok/s target. When it does, lowering the tok/s target changes nothing
  and only the P95 can shrink the fleet. Empty-looking cards are usually a
  latency promise being kept, not waste: a card sits at bandwidth x interconnect
  x MBU / achieved tok/s GB, so a fleet sized for first-token compute or for
  peak admission leaves VRAM unused by design.
- Workload presets carry SLO targets grounded in published practice; the
  evidence and a 2026 review of every preset are in docs/PRACTICES.md.
- Scripting API in the page: window.GPUscale (compute, solvePool, sloPrice,
  sloOptScan, gpuFitScan, readState, serialize, applyConfig, autoSize,
  computeProject, buildXls, buildXlsxBytes, plus the raw libraries).

## Docs

- [Live studio](https://gpuscale.net/): the tool itself; fully static HTML/JS
- [README](https://github.com/mahmoudyassine/gpu-scale-tool/blob/main/README.md): method, formulas, worked example
- [docs/PRACTICES.md](https://github.com/mahmoudyassine/gpu-scale-tool/blob/main/docs/PRACTICES.md): the serving evidence behind every workload preset
- [docs/DATA.md](https://github.com/mahmoudyassine/gpu-scale-tool/blob/main/docs/DATA.md): data schemas, effective-KV convention, solver invariants
- [Releases](https://github.com/mahmoudyassine/gpu-scale-tool/releases): changelog with rationale per version
- [Portable single file](https://gpuscale.net/dist/gpuscale_standalone.html): the whole studio in one HTML file

## Optional

- [Mirror](https://mahmoudyassine.github.io/gpuscale/): same tool, alternate host
